WooCommerce leads the list: largest extension and theme marketplace of the listed projects, named payment gateways, runs on ordinary WordPress hosting, and our WooCommerce page names a small shop owner on WordPress as its reader. Bagisto needs PHP 8.4 and Laravel 13 and usually a PHP developer for themes and extensions (our Bagisto page), so it stays second as the pick for Laravel developers. All eight fits are 'full' or 'partial', so the full-fit block is kept and only WooCommerce moves to first.
WooCommerce: catalogue, cart, checkout in WordPress; payment gateways; extension marketplace; WordPress site, hosting and security are the owner's job
WooCommerce: free plugin adding catalogue, cart and checkout to a WordPress site; subscriptions and bookings are separate extensions
Bagisto: PHP 8.4 and Laravel 13 per composer.json; theming and extension work usually calls for a PHP developer; B2B and marketplace features are separate packages
Spree: developer platform, storefront changes mean writing code; multi-tenant needs Enterprise Edition
PrestaShop README warns that upgrading to a new version is not trivial
Shopware: PHP skills needed for installation, upgrades and plugins; some features are commercial plans for on-premise shops
Which stores need a developer: Spree, Medusa, Saleor, Solidus are developer platforms; Bagisto and Shopware need a PHP developer (see research/sources/projects)
WooCommerce suits a small shop owner on WordPress or with a WordPress host; PrestaShop is a standalone PHP store
